bead.title: Add literal wire assertions to RESP post-update e2e
bead.description: PROBLEM: the RESP e2e oracle compares the stream entry to the backend's claimed_view, so the post-update check is circular and can pass even when the wire payload is wrong. ROOT CAUSE: `crates/pqueue-resp/tests/e2e.rs:283-326` updates the item through the backend and then validates the claimed stream entry with `assert_claimed_entry_parity` (`crates/pqueue-resp/tests/e2e.rs:380-444`), which never asserts the literal post-update wire values. PROPOSED FIX: add direct wire assertions for `field-a == value-a-2` and `field-c == value-c` in the claimed entry after `update_fields`, while keeping the backend-view parity check as a secondary guard. NON-SCOPE: conformance gating, postgres CI, reserved-name policy, and whole_group coverage. Parent bead pqueue-7bed1610; review basis dbf97f1/14d04ac on beads pqueue-46ea00f4 and pqueue-5c70706b.
bead.acceptance:
1. `TestRespWireCarriesUpdatedFieldAAndFieldC` asserts the RESP entry contains `field-a == value-a-2` and `field-c == value-c` after the update.
2. `TestRespOracleDoesNotUseBackendEcho` proves the wire assertion is independent of the backend's claimed_view echo.
3. `go test ./...` passes.
4. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
